news_stories: BC delivering more than $6.4 billion in new hospital construction starting 2025-2026
Quebec allocates $2.3 billion over 10 years for hospital construction in 2026-27 budget
Health care & social assistance +18,000 jobs in April 2026 LFS

cross_references.interpretation: 253 healthcare projects ($21.07B) align with BC's $6.4B program and QC's $2.3B/10yr allocation; flagship builds include New St. Paul's (1.2M sq ft) and Dawson Creek ($590M, ~92% complete)

trend_analysis.momentum: Sector GDP +2.1% Y/Y though flat M/M; +18,000 April jobs; 19 new projects in 21 days
trend_analysis.comparison: Steady Y/Y growth with hospital-construction programs adding pipeline volume; QC flags a hospital-repair backlog
trend_analysis.outlook: If BC's $6.4B program and QC's $2.3B/10yr allocation deploy as budgeted, long-term-care and cancer-centre capital would expand. The construction pipeline (253 projects) is distinct from health-service GDP output.

policy_items.title: International Convention Attraction Fund + FIFA 2026 Venue Spending
policy_items.description: ICAF secured 116 events (~324,200 attendees, $803.3M direct impact) as of March 2026; BC Place upgraded for seven FIFA World Cup 2026 matches; federal $726,000 in Corleck Building cultural space, Toronto

news_stories: BC Place upgraded to host seven FIFA World Cup 2026 matches, ~$1B additional BC visitor spending 2026-31
International Convention Attraction Fund secures 116 events ($803.3M direct impact) as of March 2026
Ontario NAICS 71 employed 177,700 (2024); Quebec job growth 2024-2026 expected negative

cross_references.magnitude: ~$1B additional BC visitor spending 2026-31; ICAF 116 events / $803.3M
cross_references.interpretation: 143 tourism_culture projects ($22B, shared with NAICS 72) intersect FIFA 2026 venue/event spending and the ICAF program; discretionary spending remains sensitive to trade tensions

trend_analysis.momentum: Sector GDP +0.2% Y/Y but -2.5% M/M; FIFA 2026 and ICAF event spending are forward demand drivers
trend_analysis.comparison: Ontario moderate-to-slow employment growth diverges from Quebec's negative 2024-2026 job-growth expectation
trend_analysis.outlook: If FIFA World Cup 2026 demand materializes as projected (~$1B BC visitor spending 2026-31), venue/event activity would rise. If trade tensions further pressure discretionary spending, the marginal Y/Y growth may erode.

servicesIndustries.name: Accommodation & Food Services
key_facts: Canada hotel construction pipeline at record Q1 2026 levels — 331 hotel projects / 45,401 rooms; Ontario leads with 190 projects / 27,567 rooms (57%); Toronto 71 projects / 11,420 rooms
Canada hospitality market USD 21.34B in 2026 (from USD 20.29B 2025) to USD 27.46B by 2031 (5.18% CAGR); ~1.9M workers (~9.5% of national employment); CoStar projects 1.9% RevPAR growth 2026
Accommodation and food services +13,000 jobs in April 2026 LFS; persistent labour shortage; reduced international-student/temporary-work permits constraining supply

policy_items.title: Hotel Construction Pipeline & FIFA 2026 Demand
policy_items.description: Record Q1 2026 pipeline of 331 hotel projects / 45,401 rooms; FIFA World Cup 2026 demand and ICAF events drive accommodation capital; labour supply constrained by reduced international-student/temporary-work permits

news_stories: Canada hotel construction pipeline at record Q1 2026 levels: 331 projects / 45,401 rooms
Ontario leads with 190 hotel projects / 27,567 rooms (57% of pipeline)
Accommodation and food services +13,000 jobs in April 2026 LFS

cross_references.interpretation: 143 tourism_culture projects ($22B, shared with NAICS 71) align with the record hotel pipeline (331 projects / 45,401 rooms) and FIFA 2026 demand; labour supply constrained by reduced permits

trend_analysis.momentum: Sector GDP +3.1% Y/Y though -0.2% M/M; +13,000 April jobs; record hotel pipeline
trend_analysis.comparison: Y/Y growth and a record construction pipeline contrast with a persistent labour shortage and reduced international-student/temporary-work permits
trend_analysis.outlook: If FIFA 2026 demand and the 45,401-room pipeline proceed, accommodation capital would expand. If permit constraints persist, labour supply may limit operating capacity even as construction advances.

news_stories: No significant standalone Other-Services capital developments this week (research-led, no discrete pipeline)
Sector tracks consumer discretionary spending pressured by trade tensions

cross_references.interpretation: No discrete pipeline (personal/repair/civic/religious organizations); sector tracks consumer discretionary spending, which the Bank of Canada outlook notes is pressured by trade tensions and slow income growth

trend_analysis.momentum: Sector GDP +0.6% Y/Y, +0.3% M/M — modest, near-flat movement
trend_analysis.comparison: Stable readings consistent with consumer-discretionary sensitivity flagged in the Bank of Canada outlook
trend_analysis.outlook: If trade tensions continue pressuring household income, Other-Services demand may stay near-flat. No discrete project pipeline to cross-reference.

Canada achieved the NATO 2% GDP defence-spending target in 2025-26
Defence Investment Agency legislation (Spring 2026) moves Defence Construction Canada under DIA

cross_references.magnitude: NATO 2% GDP target achieved 2025-26; Phase 2 housing >$3.7B
cross_references.interpretation: 207 government/defence/Indigenous projects ($82.48B) cross-reference construction and healthcare; the DIA legislation (Spring 2026) and Phase 2 military housing (>$3.7B) are the principal capital drivers

trend_analysis.momentum: Sector GDP +0.3% Y/Y, -0.5% M/M; $502.8B federal Main Estimates and >$3.7B Phase 2 housing set the fiscal envelope

trend_analysis.outlook: If the DIA legislation passes Spring 2026 and Phase 2 military housing proceeds, public-administration-linked construction would expand. The GDP series reflects government-service output, distinct from the $82.48B capital pipeline.
